transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Could you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

Yeah, hey. Thanks for seeing me. Um, I guess what finally got me to come in is... well, I'm an electrician, and lately I just can’t keep my focus on one estimate or, like, a code form anymore. 

Which reminds me, the city just changed the municipal codes again, which is a total nightmare. My buddy Mike—he does HVAC—he was telling me about it at this diner we go to on 4th street. They actually roast their own coffee beans right there in the back, it's incredible. You wouldn't think a diner would do that, but the owner is this guy from Seattle who's super obsessed with the whole roasting process... 

Wait, what was I talking about? Oh, right, the estimates. Yeah, I try to sit down and do the paperwork, but then I hear a tool noise from the garage, or I get a text, or I suddenly get some brand new idea about how to redesign my workshop. I actually bought all this new pegboard for it yesterday. But it just pulls me completely off track, and now my jobs are starting to get all mixed up.
Do you also find yourself getting distracted or having trouble focusing on tasks at home or in other situations, like during conversations or while driving?

Driving? Um, I'm not really sure, I haven't really noticed it being a problem on the road. I mean, I drive a 2012 Silverado for work, and honestly, the suspension has been driving me crazy lately. It makes this loud clanking noise whenever I hit a pothole. I took it over to my mechanic, Dave—he’s got this shop off Route 9, right behind where that old drive-in theater used to be. 

It's a huge shame they tore that down, actually. They're building all these luxury condos there now. It feels like everything in this town is just turning into condos these days. My sister just moved into one of those new complexes on the east side, and they charge her like, two grand a month just for a one-bedroom. It's completely insane, especially since the construction quality is super cheap. I was looking at the wiring in her kitchen and it's totally amateur hour. 

But, uh... wait. What did you ask me? Oh, right, getting distracted in conversations and stuff. Yeah, I don't know. I guess I haven't really paid much attention to that.
Do you often find yourself starting new projects or tasks without finishing the ones you were working on before?

Yeah, oh man, absolutely. I've been going nonstop lately. It's like I'm bouncing from job sites to doing bids, and then I'm back in my workshop rewiring test panels. I just can't stop. Like, I'll get this brilliant idea for a new home-automation setup—which is huge right now, by the way. Everyone wants their lights and their thermostat connected to their phone. 

I was actually just looking at this new smart hub system online last night. It integrates with almost everything, even older HVAC units, which is wild. My buddy Mike—the HVAC guy—he was telling me that half his calls now are just people who bought a smart thermostat off Amazon and completely botched the wiring. They cross the C-wire with the RC and blow the fuse on the control board. It’s hilarious, honestly, but it keeps him busy. He actually just bought a boat with the extra money he’s making. A little pontoon, nothing crazy, but he wants to take it out on Lake Hopatcong this weekend. 

But yeah, sitting still just feels like a complete waste of time right now. So I end up starting a new automation idea before the last one is even close to done. I just have so much energy for it all, you know?
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually confident or powerful lately, like you don’t need as much sleep or that you can take on way more than usual without getting tired?

Yeah, confident? I guess so, yeah. Like, recently I've just been feeling like I could easily take on these massive commercial jobs, you know? Like I could bid on a whole office park and just train up a massive crew to handle it right now. Even though, I mean, realistically, my licensing isn't really there yet, and I haven't done commercial scale stuff, but I just feel like I could completely crush it. 

Speaking of commercial jobs, they just broke ground on that new Amazon warehouse out by the interstate. It's supposed to be like, two million square feet or something ridiculous like that. I drove past it the other day and the amount of steel they're putting up is insane. My cousin works in logistics, and he was telling me how those warehouses are basically entirely run by robots now. The robots just zip around and grab the shelves and bring them right to the packers. It's crazy how fast automation is taking over. He actually got a job in management over there, and he's making really good money. He just bought a new jet ski, actually. We used to take his old one out to the reservoir when we were kids...

Wait, sorry. What did you ask me? Oh, right, feeling powerful and stuff. Yeah, I just feel like I can handle anything right now, even if it's way out of my league.
